title: The Circuit Solver
summary: Reduce resistor networks, balance junction currents and solve loops with Kirchhoff's rules.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can reduce series-parallel networks, apply the junction and loop rules, solve a two-loop network for currents and directions, and use symmetry on a cube of resistors.

levels.title: Reduce the network
levels.adds: Baseline: series add, parallel add reciprocals, and work from the inside out (Example 3.5).
hints: Combine the group that is purely series or purely parallel first.
Series: resistances add. Parallel: reciprocals add.
Then decide whether R₁ carries the whole current or has the whole battery across it.

levels.title: The junction rule
levels.adds: New idea: the currents into a junction equal the currents out of it (Section 3.12).
hints: Count the current going in as positive and going out as negative.
The four currents must sum to zero.
The sign of what is missing tells you the direction.

levels.title: The loop rule
levels.adds: New idea: emfs and voltage drops add to zero round a loop, with signs from the direction (Section 3.12).
hints: Go round the loop: emfs that help the current are positive, those that oppose are negative.
The total of IR drops equals the net emf.
The larger emf decides which way the current flows.

levels.title: A two-loop network
levels.adds: More steps: one junction equation and two loop equations give three unknown currents (Ex 3.7, Example 3.6).
hints: The middle current is the sum of the two outer currents.
Write the loop rule for each outer loop, using the shared resistor.
A negative answer means the current really flows the other way.

levels.title: The cube of resistors
levels.adds: Apply it: use symmetry to find R_eq of a cube of 12 resistors across opposite corners (Example 3.5).
hints: The three edges at the positive corner carry equal currents by symmetry.
At the next corners each current splits equally in two.
Apply the loop rule along one path from the positive to the negative corner.

misconceptions: Current is used up as it passes through a resistor
Resistors in parallel add their resistances
The current in a branch must flow from the positive terminal
A negative current in a Kirchhoff equation means a mistake
